WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p286/r6.claim: On this view, someone who worships only in prosperity is on one edge, while worship in both ease and hardship shows acceptance of the Creator's direction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p286/r6.anchor: ومن عبد الله على السراء وحدها دون أن # يعبده على الضراء فقد عبده على حرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p286/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p286/r7.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p286/r7.claim: Hasan identifies the person as a hypocrite who worships with his tongue but not his heart; “on an edge” then means doubt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p286/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو المنافق يعبد الله بلسانه دون قلبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r1.claim: The good that brings reassurance means prosperity, health, abundant crops, and wealth; the pronoun in “he is reassured by it” refers to that good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r1.anchor: قوله: {فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به} إن أصابه رخاء (¬5) وعافية وخصب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r2.claim: The trial means drought and loss of wealth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r3.claim: To turn on one's face means to leave religion for disbelief and idol worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r3.anchor: رجع عن دينه إلى الكفر وعبادة الأوثان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r4.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad says he turns away from the religion he had followed; “face” may mean the path from which he came, namely disbelief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r4.anchor: قلب وجهه عما كان عليه من الدين والعبادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r5.speaker: الكلبي وغيره من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r5.claim: The verse was revealed about Bedouins who came to Medina: prosperity made one praise the faith, but illness, loss, or delayed charity led Satan to make him renounce it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r5.anchor: نزلت في أعراب كانوا يقدمون على رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- المدينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r6.claim: The wavering worshipper loses worldly life by failing to obtain the wealth he sought and the afterlife by apostasy; this is the manifest loss.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r6.anchor: خسر دنياه حيث لم يظفر بما طلب من المال، وخسر آخرته بارتداده عن الدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r7.claim: The verb “he lost” itself indicates the noun “loss.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p287/r7.anchor: وخسر يدل على الخسران؛ لأن الفعل يدل على المصدر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r5.claim: Worshiping God on an edge means entering religion without settled commitment; prosperity and increased wealth reassure such people, while drought and poverty make them turn back to unbelief.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r5.anchor: على جانب لا يدخل فيه دخول متمكن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356/r7.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356/r7.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda explain worshipping God 'on an edge' as worship based on doubt.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356/r7.anchor: {ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف} [الحج: 11] تفسير مجاهد وقتادة: على شك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the doubter is content when good fortune comes but turns back as a disbeliever when hardship strikes, losing both this world and the next.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r1.anchor: {فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به} [الحج: 11] يقول رضي به.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r2.claim: Qatāda describes the good fortune as abundant harvest, comfort, and desired pleasures, which make the person claim certainty; hardship makes him abandon the truth he knew.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: يقول إن أصاب خصبا ورفاغة في العيش وما يشتهي اطمأن إليه وقال: أنا على حق وأنا أعرف الذي أنا عليه:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p356#2/r3.claim: The turn back on one's face means leaving the truth one had followed and denying that one knew it; the person loses his worldly gains and has no share in the Hereafter.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r1.claim: The worldly loss is losing the very life one worked for and enjoyed, which had been one's main concern and aim, while reaching the Hereafter with no share.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r1.anchor: {خسر الدنيا} [الحج: 11] يعني خسر دنياه التي كان لها عمل وفيها يفرح، فهي همه وطلبته،

ELMALILI:22:8-13/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r3.claim: Worshipping God “on an edge” means practicing religion from the margin for a particular aim, rather than wholeheartedly, or becoming Muslim only verbally.
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r3.anchor: Yani cân ü gönülden değil de bir kenardan, bir maksad-ı mahsus için dindarlık eder veya dil ucuyla Müslüman olur

ELMALILI:22:8-13/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r4.claim: Such a person is content when good comes but turns away when hardship tests him.
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r4.anchor: da kendisine bir hayır isabet ederse ona mutmain olur

ELMALILI:22:8-13/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r5.claim: One reported occasion of revelation names Uyaina b. Badr, Aqra b. Habis, and Abbas b. Mirdas among those who would accept Muhammad's religion if it brought them good, otherwise call it false.
ELMALILI:22:8-13/r5.anchor: müellefetü’l-kulûbdan Uyeyne b. Bedr, Akra‘b. Hâbis, Abbas b. Mirdas birbirlerine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r1.claim: The verse depicts people whose worship depends on worldly comfort: they are content when life goes well but abandon faith in hardship, seeking a god who serves their wishes; they lose both worlds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r1.anchor: imanlarına pamuk ipliğiyle bağlı olan bu tür kimselerin işleri rast gittikçe Allah’a kulluk etmekten memnun oldukları, bir imtihan sıkıntısına mâruz kaldıklarında ise hemen bu statüden sıyrılmak istedikleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r2.claim: The phrase translated as worshipping God ‘conditionally’ can also mean worshipping hesitantly, without full belief, or on the edge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r2.anchor: Allah’a şartlı olarak kulluk eder” şeklinde tercüme edilen kısmına, “Allah’a tereddütler içinde, tam inanmadan, sınırda, kıyıdan kıyıya kulluk eder” mânaları da verilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r6.speaker: rivayetler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r6.claim: Reports connect the verse’s occasion to Bedouins who converted hoping for prosperity, or a Jew who left Islam after his affairs went badly; the author says it describes a recurring human type in every age and place.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r6.anchor: refah düzeyinin artacağı ümidine bağlı olarak müslüman olan bazı bedevî Araplar’ın veya bir yahudinin İslâmiyet’i kabul ettikten sonra işlerinin ters gitmesi karşısında dinden çıkması üzerine indiği yönünde rivayetler bulunmaktadır

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r1.claim: The commentators say the verse describes Bedouin migrants whose faith depended on prosperity: health, a good horse, children, and wealth pleased them, while misfortune made them turn back.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: نزلت في أعراب كانوا يقدمون على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - المدينة مهاجرين من باديتهم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r2.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports a Jewish convert who, after losing eyesight, wealth, and children, asked to abandon Islam; the Prophet refused and compared Islam’s testing to fire refining metals.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r2.anchor: وروى عطية عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: أسلم رجل من اليهود فذهب بصره وماله وولده وتشاءم بالإسلام

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r3.claim: The Prophet compares Islam’s testing of people to fire separating the impurities of iron, silver, and gold.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p307/r3.anchor: يا يهودي إن الإسلام يسبك الرجال كما تسبك النار خبث الحديد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r3.claim: Claiming to worship God while associating partners with Him is baseless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r3.anchor: the claim of worshipping God while associating partners with Him is a baseless one

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r4.claim: The hypocrite described in the passage worships and obeys God only while apparent benefits continue, then flees in trial to seek help elsewhere and loses both this world and the next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r4.anchor: people who were indifferent to the Hereafter and wanted to always argue and dispute with the Prophet (sws) in support of polytheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r5.claim: The alleged deities sought for benefit cause more harm than good; only God has authority to harm or benefit people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r5.anchor: The harm of those to whom they run for their benefits while leaving God is more than their use.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.claim: The passage revisits monotheism and the Hereafter through human creation, cosmic signs, and divine attributes, contrasts sincere submission with conditional worship and hypocrisy, and concludes with the fate of believers and polytheists.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p168/r7.anchor: In the coming verses, the subject of monotheism and hereafter discussed earlier is brought up in another way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r2.claim: Some people worship on their own terms: they comply when directives suit their desires but evade those that conflict with their interests, becoming two-faced hypocrites.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r2.anchor: As long as His directives were in accordance with their desires, they were prepared to worship Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r3.claim: The hypocrites seek to believe in God and Satan, belief and disbelief together; their conciliatory posture is effectively polytheism, even worse than open opposition, and religion permits no such double standards.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r3.anchor: It wanted to believe in God and Satan, belief and disbelief at the same time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.claim: Those who deny that benefit and harm are in God’s hands may choose their conduct, but their strategies cannot succeed without His consent; believers and polytheists will face judgement according to belief and deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r4.anchor: the greatest of their strategies is not going to avail them without God’s consent.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r2.claim: Verse 11 turns from open advocates of polytheism to opportunists who try to maintain ties with both God and Satan, truth and falsehood; after Islam’s rise, two-faced people appeared among idolaters and the People of the Book.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r2.anchor: After mentioning the Idolaters who were prepared to argue and debate in favour of polytheism, those people are referred to who wanted to simultaneously have ties with God and Satan

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r3.claim: These opportunists sought a compromise between belief and disbelief, keeping ancestral deities for their supposed benefits; even when they entered Islam, calamity drove them to other protectors, making their posture polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r3.anchor: They reckoned that why should these beings be forsaken when they are of benefit to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r4.claim: The difference between these hypocrites and aggressive polytheist debaters is only tone; genuine monotheism requires total submission whether God grants comfort or decrees a terrible death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p177/r4.anchor: If there is a difference between the two, it is only of the tone.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r1.claim: ‘Worshipping God at one edge’ expresses disgust: worship means servitude and obedience, while ‘edge’ means from afar; such people neither fully enter Islam nor sincerely side with Muslims or disbelievers, as the cited verses illustrate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r1.anchor: The word “worship” here refers both to servitude and obedience to the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r2.claim: Fitnah means trial or calamity and explains their wavering: they are content while things suit them, but flee adversity; the path to God includes trials that must be passed to please Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r2.anchor: This portion is actually an explanation of the words “at an edge.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r3.claim: Trials that are met with submission strengthen faith and multiply future reward; those who despair of God and think ill of Him lose both worlds, while ordinary worldly loss can be recompensed in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r3.anchor: All such trials strengthen his faith and multiply his reward manifold in the hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r4.claim: The author applies the verse to Muslims today: they may revere the Qur’an ceremonially yet follow others in public and private affairs and use the Qur’an at funerals instead of as guidance for the living.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p178/r4.anchor: For them, the Qur’ ān is not a Book for the living; it is a Book for the dead.

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r2.claim: The occasion is a migrant who prospered in health, family, and livestock and praised Islam, but called it bad when illness, a daughter, financial loss, or delayed charity came.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r2.anchor: فنزلت الآية: (ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف)، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r3.claim: Another report says Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma asked the Prophet for gifts, praising Islam when given them and threatening to return to polytheism if refused.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r3.anchor: نزلت في بني أسد بن خزيمة جاءوا إلى رسول الله

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r4.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī identifies the people as hypocrites who praise religion at one time and condemn it at another.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r4.anchor: نزلت في المنافقين، عن أبي علي؛ لأنه يمدح الدين في وقت

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r5.claim: An alternative identifies weak Muslims, who may apostatize, unlike hypocrites who were always disbelievers; another says the hypocrite's alternating praise and blame is like turning over.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r5.anchor: نزلت في ضعفة المسلمين؛ لأن المسلم يكون منقلبا على وجهه بالارتداد

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r7.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r7.claim: “On an edge” means worship on a doubtful, unsteady footing; it can also mean a weak or marginal religious commitment.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r7.anchor: على ضعف في العبادة كضعف القيام على حرف

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r8.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the edge is worship by tongue without heart: religion has two parts, tongue and heart, and confession unsupported by the heart is precarious.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r8.anchor: الدين حرفان: أحدهما اللسان، والثاني القلب

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r9.claim: When worldly good arrives, such a person settles into the religion; when bodily or financial hardship comes, he reverts to disbelief and loses both worlds.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r9.anchor: فإن أصابه خير أي: صحة في بدنه وسعة في معيشته اطمأن به

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهنيئامرياكأنكقلتثبتلكهن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهنيئامرياكأنكقلتثبتلكهن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهنيئامرياكأنكقلتثبتلكهن.claim: After hearing that good befell someone, Sībawayh parses هنيئًا مريئًا as accusatives with an omitted verb, understood as ثبت ذلك له or هنأه ذلك; the verb and phrase can replace each other.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهنيئامرياكأنكقلتثبتلكهن.anchor: وإنما نصبته لأنه ذكر لك خيرا أصابه رجل فقلت هنيئا مريئا كأنك ~~قلت ثبت ذلك له هنيئا مريئا

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: Alif-lām marks class labels that apply to each member; this explains the definite collective in “from the people.”
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: من كان من أمته أو كان في صفته من الأسماء التي يدخلها الألف

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: A common epithet can become a proper name for one person, as al-Ṣaʿq did; al-Najm likewise names the Pleiades.

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: Ibn Ralān and Ibn Kurāʿ became names for particular men, so the names do not identify every son of those fathers.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: وكابن الصعق قولهم ابن رالان وابن كراع صار علما لإنسان واحد

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: Al-Khalīl says bare Zayd and ʿAmr name particular people; al-Ḥārith, al-Ḥasan, and al-ʿAbbās instead treat the person as the quality itself, while bare Ḥārith and ʿAbbās behave like Zayd.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أنه إنما منعهم أن يدخلوا في هذه

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: The stars al-Dabarān, al-Simāk, and al-ʿAyyūq retain alif-lām because each denotes a specific celestial object.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: فإنما يلزم الألف واللام من قبل أنه

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: When a star-name’s derivation is no longer known, Sibawayh attributes that gap to lost knowledge, not to a different naming rule.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: فإن كان عربيا نعرفه ولا نعرف الذي اشتق

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: Al-Arbiʿāʾ and al-Thulāthāʾ mean “the fourth” and “the third,” yet function as established proper names like Zayd and ʿAmr.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: إنما يريد الرابع والثالث وكلها أخبارها كأخبار زيد وعمرو

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: Dual forms such as two Zayds or two ʿAmrs remain indefinite when they mean any two people from those name-classes.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: زيدان منطلقان وهذان عمران منطلقان لم يكن هذا الكلام إلا نكرة

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: Dual and plural place-names such as Abānān and ʿArafāt designate particular locations and are definite, unlike arbitrary duals of personal names.

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: Fixed places and mountains can bear such dual or plural names because they remain in place; people and animals move and can be distinguished one from another.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: وليس هذا في الأناسى ولا في الدواب إنما يكون هذا في الأماكن والجبال

SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.claim: In “the year of the two ʿUmars,” alif-lām makes the otherwise indefinite dual definite, like the well-known pair of stars.
SIBAWAYH:يكونلكلمنكانمنأمتهأوكانفيصفتهمن.anchor: واما قولهم أعطيكم سنة العمرين فإنما أدخلت الألف واللام على عمرين وهما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.claim: The form faʿla can denote a kind or manner of action, as in qatlah and ṭaʿmah; Sibawayh distinguishes this use from a single occurrence.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.anchor: وذلك قولك حسن الطعمة وقتلته قتلة سوء وبئست الميتة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.claim: The same faʿla pattern does not always mean a kind of action: shidda, shaʿra, and duriya are lexical uses of the form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.anchor: وقد تجئ الفعلة لا يراد بها هذا المعنى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.claim: The phrase layta shiʿrī is a frequent, lightened expression; frequent proverbs can likewise preserve forms that would otherwise sound heavy.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.anchor: وقالوا ليت شعري في هذا الموضع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.claim: For one occurrence of an action, the regular form is faʿla directly from the verbal base, because augmented verbal nouns are not obligatory patterns for every verb.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.anchor: المرة الواحدة من الفعل جئت به أبدا على فعلة على الأصل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.claim: A single occurrence can occasionally be expressed with an established verbal noun, as in itiyāna, liqāʾa, iʿṭāʾa, and istidrāja, but this is rare.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.anchor: وقالوا أتيته إتيانة ولقيته لقاءة واحدة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.claim: Ghazāh and ḥijjah name a single campaign or pilgrimage as lexical nouns rather than using the regular faʿla pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.anchor: وقالوا غزاة فأرادوا عمل وجه واحد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.claim: Qanmah, sahkah, and khamṭah are names for kinds of wind, not nouns formed from an action verb.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتجئفيهالفعلةتريدبهاضرب.anchor: وقالوا قنمة وسهكة وخمطة جعلوه اسما لبعض الريح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.claim: A cited observation contrasts a healthy wealthy person who withholds beneficence with the same person when ill, who panics and begins making bequests.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.anchor: إذا صَحَّ الغنيُّ مَنَعَ المعروف وشَحَّ بماله، وإذا مرض جزع وأخذ يوصي

NASHR:v1p23/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p23/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
NASHR:v1p23/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says abandoning a lifelong dialect and habit would be severely difficult, so God graciously allowed latitude in languages and vocalic forms.
NASHR:v1p23/r3.anchor: (قال ابن قتيبة) : ولو أراد كل فريق من هؤلاء أن يزول عن لغته

NASHR:v1p23/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p23/r4.speaker: أهل اللغة
NASHR:v1p23/r4.claim: Linguists define ḥarf as an edge, face, side, boundary, or part; it also means an alphabetic letter as part of a word.
NASHR:v1p23/r4.anchor: حرف كل شيء طرفه ووجهه وحافته وحده وناحيته والقطعة منه

NASHR:v1p23/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p23/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p23/r5.claim: Al-Dani’s first account is that the Qur'an came in seven linguistic modes: ḥarf means a face, as in worshipping God on one face or condition in this verse.
NASHR:v1p23/r5.anchor: الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني: معنى الأحرف التي أشار إليها النبي

NASHR:v1p23/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p23/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p23/r6.claim: Al-Dani’s second account treats ḥarf as an expansive Arab label for a whole connected to one part; a reading is called a letter because one letter may change.
NASHR:v1p23/r6.anchor: أن يكون سمى القراءات أحرفا على طريق السعة كعادة العرب في تسميتهم الشيء باسم ما هو منه

NASHR:v2p325/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p325/r3.speaker: ابن مهران عن روح وزيد عن يعقوب
NASHR:v2p325/r3.claim: Ibn Mihran from Rawh and Zayd from Yaʿqub transmit an alif, making the phrase active-participial خاسر الدنيا with al-ākhirati genitive; Hamid, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin, and others read it, except Ibn Muhaysin uses accusative.
NASHR:v2p325/r3.anchor: وانفرد ابن مهران عن روح بإثبات الألف في خسر الدنيا على وزن فاعل وخفض الآخرة، وكذا روى زيد عن يعقوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.claim: Here ‘on a harf’ means in a way or manner; the worshipper's manner is doubt and hesitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r1.anchor: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف [الحج: 11] أي على وجه وطريقة، هي ريب وشك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.claim: The Prophetic explanation of seven ahruf is not the set of differences in recitation that Muslims were permitted to use.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r2.anchor: فهذا تفسير منه صلى الله عليه وسلم للأحرف السبعة، ولكن ليست هذه التي أجاز لهم القراءة بها على اختلافها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.claim: The seven ahruf in the hadith mean seven paths or modes, including permitting and prohibiting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r3.anchor: فكذلك معنى هذا الحديث على سبع طرائق، من تحليل، وتحريم، وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.claim: Ubayy reports the Prophet saying revelation expanded from one or two ahruf to seven, all sufficient; examples include divine names such as Forgiving, Merciful, Hearing, Knowing, and Wise, while punishment and mercy should not be interchanged at the ending.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «يا أبي إني أقرئت القرآن على حرف أو حرفين ثم زادني الملك حتى بلغ سبعة أحرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra is cited as transmitting a similar Prophetic report about the seven ahruf, through Thabit ibn Qasim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r5.anchor: وقد أسند ثابت بن قاسم نحو هذا الحديث عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.claim: The source also cites a similar statement from Ibn Masud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r6.anchor: وذكر من كلام ابن مسعود نحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.speaker: القاضي ابن الطيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Tayyib distinguishes these seven from the seven modes and the permitted readings, interpreting them instead as seven aspects of God's names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r7.anchor: قال القاضي ابن الطيب: «وهذه أيضا سبعة غير السبعة التي هي وجوه وطرائق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.claim: If this report is established, its unrestricted permission is understood as an original rule that was later abrogated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r8.anchor: وإذا ثبتت هذه الرواية حمل على أن هذا كان مطلقا ثم نسخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r9.claim: People may not replace a name of God in its place with another name, whether the substitute has the same meaning or a different one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r9.anchor: فلا يجوز للناس أن يبدلوا اسما لله في موضع بغيره مما يوافق معناه أو يخالفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r10.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r10.claim: One group claims every word with variant readings has seven forms, otherwise the hadith's meaning would fail.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r10.anchor: وزعم قوم أن كل كلمة تختلف القراءة فيها فإنها على سبعة أوجه، وإلا بطل معنى الحديث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r11.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r11.claim: That group says some of the forms are known through transmitted reports, while others remain unknown when no report conveys them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r11.anchor: قالوا: «وتعرف بعض الوجوه بمجيء الخبر به، ولا نعرف بعضها، إذا لم يأت به خبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r12.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r12.claim: Another group says the hadith requires one or two Qur'anic words to be read in seven forms; that would fulfill its meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r12.anchor: وقال قوم: ظاهر الحديث يوجب أن يوجد في القرآن كلمة أو كلمتان تقرءان على سبعة أوجه، فإذا حصل ذلك تم معنى الحديث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r13.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r13.claim: A group interprets the hadith as saying the Qur'an was revealed in seven different languages.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r13.anchor: وقد زعم قوم أن معنى الحديث أنه نزل على سبع لغات مختلفات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r14.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r14.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib rejects seven distinct languages, except alternative forms within one story; ʿUmar, Ubayy, Hishām ibn Ḥakīm, and Ibn Masʿūd shared one language despite differing readings and disputing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43#2/r14.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب: «وقد زعم قوم أن معنى الحديث أنه نزل على سبع لغات مختلفات وهذا باطل إلا أن يريد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r1.claim: The author says fellow believers among the learned, eloquent, and people of justice repeatedly sought his interpretation after hearing him uncover some of its truths, and wanted a work gathering such insights.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r1.anchor: كلما رجعوا الي في تفسير آية فأبرزت لهم بعض الحقائق من الحجب أفاضوا في الاستحسان والتعجب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r2.claim: They proposed a commentary titled Kashf ʿan ḥaqāʾiq al-tanzīl wa-ʿuyūn al-aqāwīl fī wujūh al-taʾwīl; he declined, but they persisted and appealed through religious leaders and scholars.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r2.anchor: مقترحين ان املى عليهم الكشف عن حقائق التنزيل وعيون الأقاويل في وجوه التأويل فاستعفيت فأبوا الا المراجعة والاستشفاع بعظماء الدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r3.claim: He considered answering a duty incumbent on each person, but hesitated because of his era’s poor conditions, weak people, and lack of ambition or ability for the demanding foundations of rhetoric.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r3.anchor: والذي حداني على الاستعفاء على علمي انهم طلبوا ما الإجابة اليه على واجبه لأنه الخوض فيه كفرض العين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r4.claim: He had dictated a discussion of the Qurʾānic openings and a substantial treatment of al-Baqara in question-and-answer form, intending to show the richness of the discipline and offer a model to follow.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r4.anchor: فأمليت عليهم مسألة في الفواتح وطائفة من الكلام في حقائق سورة البقرة وكان كلاما مبسوطا كثير السؤال والجواب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r5.claim: After deciding to return to God’s sanctuary and travel to Mecca, he found in each town people eager to see and learn from the earlier dictation; their eagerness renewed his activity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r5.anchor: فتوجهت تلقاء مكة وجدت في مجتازي بكل بلد من فيه مسكة من أهلها وقليل ما هم عطشى الكباد إلى العثور على ذلك المملى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r6.claim: In Mecca he met the noble imam Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ḥamza ibn Wahhās, a distinguished descendant of al-Ḥasan, exceptionally eager for the work and so intent that he had considered traveling to Khwarazm to obtain it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r6.anchor: الأمير الشريف الامام شرف آل رسول الله أبي الحسن علي بن حمزة بن وهاس أدام الله مجده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r7.claim: The author says he was advanced in age when he finally undertook this renewed effort.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p43/r7.anchor: ورأيتني قد اخذت مني السن وتقعقع الشن وناهزت العشر التى سمتها العرب دقاقة الرقاب

TAB-FULL:v1p73/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r1.claim: In several reports Ibn Abbas attributes to the Prophet a warning that one who speaks about the Qur’an by opinion or without knowledge should prepare for Hell; the wording varies, and al-Ṭabarī gives no grading.
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «من قال في القرآن برأيه، فليتبوأ مقعده من النار»

TAB-FULL:v1p73/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r2.claim: Abu Bakr says he would have no refuge if he spoke about the Qur’an without knowledge; another version specifies opinion or what one does not know.
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه: «أي أرض تقلني، وأي سماء تظلني، إذا قلت في القرآن ما لا أعلم»

TAB-FULL:v1p73/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī holds that interpretation whose knowledge depends on the Prophet’s explicit text or evidence he established may not be stated from personal opinion.
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r3.anchor: إلا بنص رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أو بنصبه الدلالة عليه، فغير جائز لأحد القيل فيه برأيه

TAB-FULL:v1p73/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r4.claim: Even a guess that happens to reach the correct meaning is still a mistaken act, since it is conjecture rather than certain knowledge and asserts about God what one does not know.
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r4.anchor: لأن إصابته ليست إصابة موقن أنه محق، وإنما هو إصابة خارص وظان

TAB-FULL:v1p73/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī grounds this ban in 7:33, where God forbids people to say about Him what they do not know.
TAB-FULL:v1p73/r5.anchor: وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون} [الأعراف: 33]

TAB-FULL:v1p83/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r1.claim: God’s command that the Prophet deliver revelation and make it known shows it was sent down for him to explain to people.
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r1.anchor: أنه إنما نزل إليه ما أنزل، ليبين للناس ما نزل إليهم

TAB-FULL:v1p83/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Companions would not move beyond ten learned verses until they understood their meanings and acted on them.
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r2.anchor: وصحة الخبر عن عبد الله بن مسعود لقيله: «كان الرجل منا إذا تعلم عشر آيات، لم يجاوزهن حتى يعلم معانيهن والعمل بهن»

TAB-FULL:v1p83/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r3.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the inference that the report from ʿĀʾisha means the Prophet explained only a handful of Qur’anic verses; his mission was to explain revelation to people.
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r3.anchor: الخبر الذي ذكرنا، عن عائشة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه لم يفسر من القرآن شيئا إلا آيا تعد

TAB-FULL:v1p83/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the ʿĀʾisha report cannot serve as proof because its transmitter Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Zubayrī is unknown among hadith authorities.
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r4.anchor: راويه ممن لا يعرف في أهل الآثار، وهو جعفر بن محمد الزبيري

TAB-FULL:v1p83/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r5.claim: Those who abstained from legal verdicts still believed religion was completed before the Prophet’s death and every case had a ruling grounded in a text or indication.
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r5.anchor: لم يقبض نبيه إليه إلا بعد إكمال الدين به لعباده، وعلمه بأن لله في كل نازلة وحادثة، حكما موجودا، بنص أو دلالة

TAB-FULL:v1p83/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains that early scholars avoided Qur’anic interpretation from fear of failing to reach the right answer, just as some feared falling short in legal reasoning; they did not regard interpretation as inaccessible to the learned.
TAB-FULL:v1p83/r6.anchor: فكذلك معنى إحجام من أحجم عن القيل في تأويل القرآن، وتفسيره من العلماء السلف، إنما كان إحجامه عنه حذار أن لا يبلغ أداء ما كلف

BAQILLANI:v1p220/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r1.claim: Al-Buhturi calls such polished lines veins of gold and shows technical mastery, yet Baqillani finds their ornament can conceal weaknesses in imagery and meaning.
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r1.anchor: وكان البحتري يسمي نحو هذه الأبيات عروق الذهب وفي نحوه ما يدل على براعته في الصناعة وحذقه في البلاغة

BAQILLANI:v1p220/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r2.claim: The lightning-like khayal imagery is overworked: linking its light to the subterranean depths of Batn Wajrah is a flaw, since faint light does not affect what lies below ground.
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r2.anchor: وهذا غلو في الصنعة إلا أن ذكره بطن وجره حشو وفي ذكره خلل

BAQILLANI:v1p220/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r3.claim: Naming several landmarks to locate the scene is padding; Baqillani compares it to Imru al-Qays giving four boundaries as if he feared a property sale would fail for want of a boundary.
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r3.anchor: وتحديده المكان - على الحشو - أحمد من تحديد امرئ القيس من ذكر

BAQILLANI:v1p220/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r4.claim: He rejects reading the line as a new flash of lightning from the beloved's direction: that break damages the praised poetic order, and the image adds no useful information.
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقدر مقدر أن البحتري قطع الكلام الأول وابتدأ بذكر برق لمع من ناحية حبيبه

BAQILLANI:v1p220/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r5.claim: The quoted pilgrimage stanza has artful openings and endings and sweet wording, but little semantic content or benefit.
BAQILLANI:v1p220/r5.anchor: هذه ألفاظ بديعة المطالع والمقاطع حلوة المجاني والمواقع قليلة المعاني والفوائد

BURHAN:v1p216/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p216/r1.speaker: ابن عبد البر
BURHAN:v1p216/r1.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr transmits a report from Ibn Masud, attributed to the Prophet, that earlier scripture came one way while the Quran came in seven categories such as commands, prohibitions, lawful and unlawful rulings, clear and ambiguous passages, and parables.
BURHAN:v1p216/r1.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر وفى ذلك حديث رواه ابن مسعود مرفوعا قال كان الكتاب الأول نزل من باب واحد على وجه واحد

BURHAN:v1p216/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p216/r2.speaker: ابن عبد البر
BURHAN:v1p216/r2.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says scholars agree the Ibn Masud report is weak; al-Baqillani takes its seven categories as aspects, not the seven licensed reading variants.
BURHAN:v1p216/r2.anchor: قال وهو حديث عند أهل العلم لا يثبت وهو مجمع على ضعفه وذكره القاضى أبو بكر بن الطيب

BURHAN:v1p216/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p216/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p216/r3.claim: Al-Baqillani says the prophetic phrase means seven aspects or methods, using على حرف in the sense of an aspect, and does not define the permitted reading variants.
BURHAN:v1p216/r3.anchor: وقال هذا التفسير منه صلى الله عليه وسلم للأحرف السبعة ولكن ليست هذه التى أجاز لهم القراءة بها على اختلافها

BURHAN:v1p216/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p216/r4.speaker: أحمد بن أبي عمران
BURHAN:v1p216/r4.claim: Ahmad ibn Abi Imran rejects this interpretation: it would absurdly imply that all Quranic content is one category such as lawful, unlawful, or parables; al-Tahawi agrees.
BURHAN:v1p216/r4.anchor: قد رده من أهل النظر منهم أحمد بن أبي عمران قال من أوله بهذا فهو فاسد لأنه محال أن يكون الحرف منها حراما

BURHAN:v1p216/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p216/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v1p216/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the interpretation weak because these categories are not called letters, and consensus excludes changing rulings or meanings.
BURHAN:v1p216/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية هذا القول ضعيف لأن هذه لا تسمى أحرفا وأيضا فالإجماع على أن التوسعة لم تقع فى تحريم حلال

BURHAN:v1p216/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p216/r6.speaker: الماوردي
BURHAN:v1p216/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi calls it wrong because the report concerns substituting one letter for another, while Muslims agree that a verse of parables cannot replace a verse of rulings.
BURHAN:v1p216/r6.anchor: وقال الماوردى هذا القول خطأ لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أشار إلى جواز القراءة بكل واحد من الحروف وإبدال حرف بحرف

BURHAN:v1p216/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p216/r7.speaker: البيهقي
BURHAN:v1p216/r7.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits the report as disconnected and calls that chain good, though Abu Salama did not meet Ibn Masud; if sound, seven means aspects, distinct from the seven reading allowances.
BURHAN:v1p216/r7.anchor: وقال البيهقى فى المدخل وقد روى هذا عن أبى سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن ابن مسعود عن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم قال هذا مرسل جيد

BURHAN:v2p211/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p211/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p211/r6.claim: The source lists these phrases as examples of rare or unusual Quranic vocabulary treated in works on غريب القرآن.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r1.claim: The written ل and ا in لا touch at their middles while their heads point apart, yielding an apt visual likeness to two people pressed together.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r1.anchor: لأن خطى اللام والألف في لا ترى رأسيهما في جهتين وتراهما قد تماسا من الوسط

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r2.claim: Jurjānī reads al-Mutanabbī’s intention as close compression and contact, not the literal posture of an embrace; another verse similarly depicts tight joining.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r2.anchor: فأما قصد المتنبي فليس بصفة عناق على الحقيقة وإنما هو تضام وتلاصق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r3.speaker: القاضي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r3.claim: The judge treats al-Mutanabbī’s image as an independent idea rather than one taken from the earlier comparison of a writer’s lām embracing an alif; borrowing would still be defensible.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r3.anchor: وذهب القاضي في بيت المتنبي إلى أنه كأنه معنى مفرد غير ماخوذ من قوله كما تعانق لام الكاتب الألفا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r4.claim: Jurjānī says the judge’s distinction does not affect his example: al-Mutanabbī’s added merit lies in hyperbolic thinness and its apt model, not in composite simile or a claim about poetic theft.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p176/r4.anchor: وهذا التفضيل والتفصيل من قول القاضي ليس قادحا في غرضى لأنى أردت أن أريك مثالا في وضع التشبيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r1.claim: Jurjānī rejects the loose common use of استعارة and restricts it to a transfer based on simile for the sake of hyperbole.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r1.anchor: وليس هذا المذهب بالمذهب المرضى بل الصواب ان تقصر الاستعارة على ما نقله نقل التشبيه للمبالغة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r2.speaker: الآمدى
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r2.claim: Al-Āmidī casually calls using المجلس for the people assembled there metaphor while discussing al-Buḥturī’s verse about a gathering place.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r2.anchor: أبا القاسم الآمدى قال في أثناء فصل يبحث عن شيء اعترض به على البحتري

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r3.claim: Using المجلس for the gathered people is based on contiguity between a place and its occupants, not resemblance; casual wording does not set the technical definition.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r3.anchor: وليس المجلس إذا وقع على القوم من طريق التشبيه بل على وجه وقوع الشيء على ما يتصل به

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r4.speaker: الآمدى
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r4.claim: In a formal classification, al-Āmidī lists metaphor with antithesis and paronomasia among the figures of badīʿ, supporting Jurjānī’s restricted technical sense.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r4.anchor: وقال الآمدى نفسه ثم قد يأتي في الشعر ثلاثة أنواع أخر يكتسي المعنى العام بها بهاء وحسنا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r5.claim: Jurjānī likens metaphor to a loan: the original owner’s claim remains, and the transferred word still depends on its source, especially when hyperbole makes a man into a lion, sea, or moon.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p349/r5.anchor: إن ملك المعير لا يزول عن المستعار واستحقاقه إياه لا يرتفع فالعارية إنما كانت عارية لأن يد المستمير
